name: Alaska
overview: Alaska has no county governments: property tax is levied by organized boroughs and by some cities, and each of them collects its own delinquent taxes. There is no tax lien or certificate sale; instead the borough or city petitions the Superior Court for a judgment and decree of foreclosure against the delinquent parcels, and the foreclosure list shows the taxes plus penalty, interest and costs owed. Owners can redeem during a one-year redemption period, and property that is not redeemed is deeded to the borough or city by the clerk of the court. The borough or city then sells property it acquired this way on its own schedule (Anchorage by sealed bid, Mat-Su online, Kenai by public outcry auction), and the deed carries no title guarantee.

counties.next_sale_note: No upcoming sale posted. The most recent was the second 2026 sale, held September 16, 2026 (past): 'A Second 2026 Tax-Foreclosed Property Sale took place September 16, 2026.' The Assembly must approve a list before a sale is announced.
counties.how_to_bid: The Municipality sells tax-foreclosed property by sealed bid after the Anchorage Assembly approves a list. Bids are hand-delivered between 8am and 3pm on the published sale date; electronic and mail-in bids are not accepted. Each bid needs a deposit of at least 25% of the bid amount (no cash, personal or company checks), which becomes non-refundable once the purchase agreement is signed. The balance is due by 5 pm on the second Friday after bid closing, by certified check or money order. Property is sold as is and the deed does not guarantee clear title.
